chunks: Muhammad ibn Hammam narrated to us, saying: Humeed ibn Ziyad al-Kufi narrated to us, saying: al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'a narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Maythami, from Za'ida ibn Qudama, from Abdul Kareem, who said:

Al-Qa'im was mentioned before Abu Abdillah, so he said: 'How can that be, and yet the orbit has not turned, until it is said: He has died or perished, or which valley has he followed?' I said: 'And what is the turning of the orbit?' He said: 'The disagreement of the Shia among themselves.'

key_terms.الْفَلَكُ: The orbit/sphere, used metaphorically for time or the course of events
key_terms.الْقَائِمِ: The Riser/Imam (referring to Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Mahdi)

ai.seo_question: What does 'the turning of the orbit' mean in the context of the Imam's reappearance?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Nu'mani's *Kitab al-Ghayba*, Imam al-Sadiq interprets the esoteric phrase 'the orbit has not turned' as a metaphor for the doctrinal fragmentation and internal discord within the Shia community, serving as a key indicator of the Imam's continued occultation. This interpretation highlights the Shia scholarly tradition of linking cosmic or temporal signs to the spiritual and communal state of the believers, emphasizing that unity is a prerequisite for the appearance of the Qa'im.
